paragraphs.en: Table 2:    Compounds according to the invention of the general formula (I), in which the substituents and symbols have the following meanings:
paragraphs.notes: The zh field holds the verbatim German, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese. 'Tabelle 2:' is printed in bold and separated from the rest of the line by a wide tab-like gap, kept here as run-on spaces. The formula reference is a capital I in parentheses. This is the caption of a new table and it fixes the shared substituents for every row of the table lower down the page.

paragraphs.notes: The block of substituent definitions printed under the Tabelle 2 caption, laid out in three columns and four rows, centred on the page. It is chemical symbols only with no German prose in it, so zh and en are the same string. Printed with superscripts throughout: R with superscript 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, the last of these taking the values R with superscript 7a and R with superscript 7b; OR with superscript 12. Y, Z, v and w are printed on the baseline with no superscript. The 2 of SO2Me and of both CH2 values is printed as a subscript. Reading order recorded here is left to right along each printed row, which is how the three columns are aligned on the page. A small stray ink blob sits above and just right of the H of 'R4 = H'; it is a scan artifact, not a superscript character, and the same blob shape recurs in the right margin of the preceding page.

paragraphs.notes: Markush enumeration table, recorded as one paragraph per the pass instructions. The cells are compound numbers and substituent symbols, not German prose, so zh and en are the same string. The header row is printed on a grey-shaded band with superscripts: R with superscript 7a, R with superscript 7b, R with superscript 12, R with superscript 1; Nr. and L carry no superscript. This table has no Physikalische Daten column, unlike Tabelle 1a and Tabelle 1b on the preceding pages. All fifteen rows carry L = CH2 and R1 = O-c-Hexyl; the R7a/R7b pairs cycle H/H, H/Me, Me/Me and the R12 values cycle Bz, PhC(O)CH2, 4-Me-Bz, MeSO2, EtSO2. The 2 in CH2, PhC(O)CH2, MeSO2 and EtSO2 is printed as a subscript. 'O-c-Hexyl' is printed with hyphens exactly as shown, the lower-case c denoting cyclo. The table is complete on this page: the header row sits directly under the scaffold drawing, the last row is Nr. 44, a ruled bottom border closes the table below it and the lower fifth of the page is blank. Although this is the first page of Tabelle 2, its compound numbering starts at 30 rather than at 1, continuing the numbering of the earlier tables; recorded as printed and not renumbered.

structures.position_in_drawing: 1st and only, centred between the block of substituent definitions and the head of the table
structures.core: Two rings joined by a ketone bridge. LEFT: a six-membered carbocycle drawn as a hexagon with two vertical sides, carrying one ring C=C and one exocyclic ring C=O, that is the enol-ether form of a cyclohexane-1,3-dione. RIGHT: a benzene ring drawn as a hexagon with two vertical sides and three inner Kekule lines. This is the Tabelle 2 scaffold: the general formula (I) with Y, Z, v, w, R2, R3, R4 and R5 already fixed by the caption block above it, leaving R7a, R7b, R12, L and R1 open for the table rows to supply.
substituents: LEFT RING, top vertex: OR12, bond drawn straight up to the label O R with superscript 12
LEFT RING, upper-right vertex: the bridging carbonyl carbon C(=O)Ar, bond drawn up-right; a ring C=C is drawn between this vertex and the OR12-bearing top vertex, as an inner parallel line
LEFT RING, lower-right vertex: =O, double bond drawn down-right to a capital O
LEFT RING, bottom vertex: a bare CH2 vertex, no substituent drawn
LEFT RING, lower-left vertex: carries BOTH R7a and R7b. R7a is drawn to the left as a bold solid wedge widening away from the ring; R7b is drawn straight down as a plain line.
LEFT RING, upper-left vertex: a bare CH2 vertex, no substituent drawn
BRIDGE: carbonyl carbon between the two rings, =O drawn straight up to a capital O, single bonds down-left to the left ring's upper-right vertex and down-right to the benzene ipso carbon
BENZENE C1 (upper-left vertex): the bridging C(=O)
BENZENE C3 (upper-right vertex): L, bonded onward to R1, drawn as -L-R1 running out to the right
BENZENE C4 (lower-right vertex): S carrying two double-bonded O drawn below it and a CH3 to its upper right, that is a methylsulfonyl SO2CH3 group
BENZENE C5 (bottom vertex): bare, no substituent drawn
BENZENE C6 (lower-left vertex): bare, no substituent drawn
BENZENE Kekule double bonds drawn as inner lines on C1=C6 (left vertical side), C2=C3 and C4=C5

drawings.notes: No arrows and no reagent labels: a single generic scaffold, drawn once above the table so that each numbered row can supply R7a, R7b, R12, L and R1. name and smiles are null because R7a, R7b, R12, L and R1 remain placeholders, so no atom set is determined by the drawing. presented_as is 'intermediate_structure' because the enum offers no value for 'a Markush scaffold heading a table of worked compounds'; it is emphatically NOT prior art, the caption directly above calls these 'Erfindungsgemäße Verbindungen', compounds according to the invention. Ring positions were read off the drawing geometry only. The benzene numbering used here takes the bridging carbonyl as C1 and runs clockwise; on that numbering the drawn Cl sits at C2 and the drawn SO2CH3 at C4, which matches the substituent map of the general formula (I) as drawn on printed page 2 of this document, where R2 sits at benzene C2 and R3 at benzene C4. The left ring is drawn as a plain six-membered ring with no repeat bracket and no Y, Z or v labels, consistent with the caption fixing Y = CH2, Z = CH2 and v = 1. The bold wedge on R7a runs from the ring carbon outward; since R7a and R7b are both placeholders and that ring carbon carries nothing else to distinguish it, the wedge does not fix a configuration and none is inferred here.

discrepancies.what: The caption block defines Z = CH2, but one carbon of the drawn left ring carries two substituents R7a and R7b rather than two hydrogens.
discrepancies.drawing_says: the lower-left vertex of the six-membered left ring bears R7a as a bold wedge to the left and R7b as a plain line downward, so that carbon has no drawn hydrogens
discrepancies.text_says: Z = CH2, with w = 2, in the caption block directly above the drawing
